title: Linkability of continuous sensor data
description: Continuous capture of heart rate, steps, GPS and timestamps allows linking of the wearer's activities, locations and health patterns over time.

title: Identifiability via GPS and timestamps
description: GPS position combined with timestamps in the telemetry flow can uniquely identify the individual wearer.

title: Disclosure of sensitive health and location data
description: The wearable device (process) receives and processes highly sensitive personal data including heart rate and precise GPS positions.

title: Unawareness of continuous telemetry sharing
description: The user (wearer) may not fully realize the privacy implications of continuously sharing detailed sensor data simply by wearing the device.

title: Explicit disclosure of personal fitness and location data
description: Wearable device (P1) shares exercise sessions, GPS traces, device id and timestamps with the companion app, transferring sensitive personal data across the device-app boundary which may violate data minimality if more data is synced than strictly required for core features.

title: Identifiability via persistent device identifier in received batches
description: Companion app (P2) receives data containing a device id combined with GPS traces and timestamps, enabling easy re-identification and long-term tracking of the individual user across multiple syncs.

title: Unawareness when manually sharing sensitive health data
description: The wearer manually enters calorie intake, meals, and weight into the companion app without being fully aware of potential privacy implications, such as how the app may process, store, or further share this personal health information.

title: Disclosure of sensitive logged health entries
description: The companion app receives and processes manually logged calorie, meal, and weight data, creating a risk of unauthorized disclosure of this sensitive personal health information if stored or handled without adequate protections.
assumptions: Assumes the app stores the entries persistently after receipt.
uncertainty_note: Citation approximate; Dd.1.1 inferred from standard LINDDUN disclosure threats for health data flows.

title: Explicit data disclosure by app when writing health logs
description: The Companion Mobile App intentionally transfers sensitive personal health data (calorie intake, weight history, exercise sessions) to the Health Log Store, which may be considered avoidable or excessive if minimality principle is not followed.
assumptions: Data is personal and identifiable health information.

title: Data disclosure in transit for health logs
description: Health log data in transit over the flow DF4 could be intercepted or disclosed if not properly encrypted, leading to unintended exposure of personal health information.
assumptions: Flow may traverse networks or shared resources.
uncertainty_note: Context does not specify encryption details.

title: Storage leading to potential data disclosure
description: The Health Log Store receives and stores detailed health logs, risking disclosure to unauthorized parties or third parties if access controls or retention policies violate minimality.
assumptions: Store may be queried or accessed beyond the app.

title: Explicit disclosure of location traces to storage
description: The Companion Mobile App (P2) writes GPS location traces with timestamps to the Location History Store, intentionally transferring sensitive personal location data across a system boundary into persistent storage.

title: Linkability of user movements via stored history
description: The Location History Store receives and retains timestamped GPS traces, enabling long-term linking of the user's location data to identify movement patterns, routines, or frequent locations.

title: Identifiability from metadata in location flow
description: The data flow carries precise GPS coordinates and timestamps, which are inherently identifying and can be used to single out the individual even without additional identifiers.

title: Explicit disclosure of sensitive health logs
description: Health Log Store (DS1) transfers detailed calorie, weight, and exercise logs to the Analytics Service, constituting an explicit data disclosure of personal health information across a system boundary.
assumptions: The data is personal and sensitive; transfer is by design but must satisfy minimality.

title: User unawareness of cross-session analytics
description: Health Analytics Service (P3) processes logs across sessions for health-condition analysis without ensuring data subjects are aware of or have consented to this specific secondary use.
assumptions: Users may not have been informed about analytics processing details.
uncertainty_note: Context does not specify consent mechanisms; inferred from typical health app scenarios.

title: Linkability via session-spanning health data
description: The data flow carries logs across multiple sessions, enabling linkability of a user's health activities over time through the combination of calorie, weight, and exercise records.
assumptions: No pseudonymization or aggregation applied at flow level.

title: Excessive location data disclosure to analytics
description: The Health Analytics Service receives full location history across sessions, enabling derivation of daily routines and movement patterns. This constitutes avoidable disclosure of highly sensitive personal data beyond strict minimality, as only aggregated or anonymized summaries might suffice for analytics.
assumptions: The query returns raw or detailed history rather than pre-aggregated results.

title: Linkability of sessions via location history flow
description: The data flow carries location history across multiple sessions, allowing the analytics service to link records and reconstruct user routines and movement patterns, increasing linkability of the individual's activities over time.
uncertainty_note: Context does not explicitly cover cross-session linkability but flow description directly implies it.

title: User unawareness of routine profiling
description: Users may be unaware that their stored location history is being queried and processed to derive detailed daily routines and movement patterns, violating informed consent principles.
assumptions: No explicit user notification or consent mechanism for this specific analytics use is described.

title: Insufficient cybersecurity risk management for health insights return flow
description: The return of sensitive inferred health-condition risk indicators, summaries and trend flags over DF8 lacks evidence of proper cybersecurity controls, creating non-compliance risk at the intersection of privacy and security for personal health data.
assumptions: Health data is subject to strict regulations (e.g. HIPAA/GDPR) requiring strong protection in transit and processing.
uncertainty_note: Context provides Nc.3 but no flow-specific details; applicability inferred from health data sensitivity.

title: Potential unauthorized disclosure of sensitive health indicators
description: The Companion Mobile App displays trends and inferred condition indicators (eating-disorder or diabetes risk signals) on the user dashboard. This sensitive personal health data could be disclosed to bystanders via shoulder-surfing or if the device screen is left visible/unlocked, as the app does not appear to implement additional display protections.

title: User unawareness of privacy implications of displayed inferences
description: The user (wearer) receives displayed inferences about eating-disorder or diabetes risks without sufficient context or warnings about how this sensitive information might be used, stored, or the broader privacy risks involved in such health inferences.
uncertainty_note: Context does not explicitly detail user notification mechanisms; inferred from flow description.

title: Disclosure of full health and location dataset to third-party cloud
description: The Health Analytics Service shares the complete sensitive health and location dataset with the Cloud Hosting Provider for hosting and replication, violating data minimality as only necessary data should be disclosed to third parties.
assumptions: Health and location data qualifies as personal/sensitive data under privacy regulations.

title: Third-party storage and replication of full dataset
description: The Cloud Hosting Provider receives, stores, and replicates the full health and location dataset, enabling potential further disclosures or access by the provider.
assumptions: The external entity may access or process the data beyond intended hosting.
uncertainty_note: Depends on contractual controls not specified in flow.

title: Transfer of analytics data and models across trust boundary
description: Analytics data, models, and full dataset transferred to external cloud, constituting explicit data disclosure to a third party.
